name: psrr-vs-freq-50ma
description: PSRR vs frequency at the 50 mA full-load condition, 1kHz and 100kHz spec points called out
claim: README.md Target specification, 'PSRR' row (DR-0004 amendment A7): >50dB @ 1kHz and >20dB @ 100kHz, C_eff=1uF nominal -- evaluated here at the 50 mA FULL-LOAD condition. This is the load condition sim/psrr-vs-freq/ disclosed as an open gap: that deck is scoped to the 1 mA light-load point (the binding one per README.md note 1) and its tb_psrr.spice header records why the two load points cannot share one deck -- ngspice's per-.meas result vectors go out of scope as soon as a later analysis becomes the current plot, so an 'alter'-and-re-.ac deck silently re-reports the first .ac's numbers. This slug closes that gap the way sim/dropout-vs-load/ already handles its own fixed full-load point: a sibling experiment with the same DUT, the same stimulus and output network, the same full PVT sweep, and its own record carrying its own separate verdict. The two verdicts are deliberately NOT merged -- read this record for the 50 mA condition and sim/psrr-vs-freq/'s record for the 1 mA condition. The load sink is the compliance-limited sink #46 introduced (Vilc/Bload/Vlmeas): it draws its commanded current for VOUT well above ground and nothing at or below it, which deletes the sink-sustained unphysical sub-ground DC solution #40 found rather than biasing the solver away from it. That solution is the dominant risk at this load -- a larger demanded current biases the unphysical root harder -- so dc_vout_v and dc_iload_ma below read the .op plot and are gated at every corner: a PSRR number is only admissible as evidence if the operating point it was linearized about is the physical one and the sink really delivered 50 mA. No ratified threshold was changed by this experiment. Update (#174, 2026-09-05, spec/decision-records/DR-0021): ldo_core's VREF was promoted from an internal net -- driven by Vref1, an ideal 1.2 V vsource instantiated INSIDE the subcircuit -- to a seventh top-level port, and the identical ideal source moved into this deck. No device was added, removed or resized, so this is an electrical no-op by construction: an ideal vsource is an ideal vsource wherever it is declared, its return was already the cell's VSS port, and it is an AC short to ground in both placements. It is not asserted on that argument alone -- origin/main at ec9e530 was extracted to a scratch tree and this bench was run on BOTH trees back to back, on the same host with the same ngspice and the same pinned PDK, and the per-corner measurement lines compared field by field; DR-0021's 'Evidence' section tabulates the result. Records minted from this deck before 2026-09-05 carry the pre-#174 six-port DUT netlist sha and are superseded on that ground alone, not because any number in them was wrong; per sim/README.md's append-only rule they are left untouched. Update (#325, 2026-09-24, carrying #304's measurement across from sim/psrr-vs-freq): the 'deletes' sentence above is scoped deliberately -- the compliance bound deletes the SINK-SUSTAINED sub-ground root and nothing else. Below the knee the sink is exactly 0 A and 0 S (f(VOUT) underflows to 0.0 in IEEE double for every VOUT <= -0.7530773732699249 V), so the load network is absent from the DC equations there: a sub-ground dc_vout_v reported together with dc_iload_ma = 0 is outside the bound's reach by construction, and no knee or softness value can delete it because the sink has no term left in the equations to remove. The sibling 1 mA deck reported exactly that at fs_125c_3.63v in record 20260923-084323-a6c95f8 (dc_vout_v = -64.75 V, dc_iload_ma = 0) on the DUT netlist of the day, and #304 measured the mechanism: not a second physical solution but a false convergence on the continuation ladder's first rung (dynamic gmin stepping), accepted by SPICE's RELATIVE convergence test 64 V from ground. That is why dc_vout_v and dc_iload_ma are gated as a PAIR rather than either one alone -- a sub-ground reading alongside the COMMANDED current is the sink-sustained root the bound deletes, alongside ZERO delivered current it is a state the bound was never in a position to delete. The deck is deliberately unchanged on that account: #304 measured that knee tuning is coin-flipping (a strictly LOOSER bound 'fixes' the same corner, so the knee is not the mechanism) and that a load-side sub-ground clamp is worse still (it adds a genuine root at VOUT = -0.4994 V that a cold start reaches). See sim/harness/README.md, 'What the bound cannot reach', for the evidence and for the reltol-ladder recipe that tells a false convergence from a genuine second root.
analyses: meas ac vout_1k FIND vdb(vout) AT=1k
meas ac vout_100k FIND vdb(vout) AT=100k

operating_conditions.load_current: 50 mA (full-load condition of the ratified PSRR row), commanded through a compliance-limited sink (Vilc/Bload/Vlmeas) and verified by dc_iload_ma
operating_conditions.output_cap: 1.0 uF nominal + 100 mOhm ESR (PSRR row's stated C_eff)
operating_conditions.enable_state: enabled (EN tied to VIN at instantiation)

psrr_1k_db.description: README.md PSRR target: >50 dB @ 1 kHz, applied at the 50 mA full-load point

psrr_100k_db.description: README.md PSRR target: >20 dB @ 100 kHz, applied at the 50 mA full-load point

dc_iload_ma.description: Harness integrity, not a ratified spec line: the compliance-limited sink must deliver the commanded 50 mA at the operating point this .ac is expanded about (see Claim)

dc_vout_v.description: Harness integrity, not a ratified spec line (the ratified accuracy row is sim/mc-output-accuracy's): asserts the .ac was linearized about the physical operating point, not the sub-ground root #40 found nor the sub-ground false convergence #304 characterised. Read it together with dc_iload_ma, which discriminates the two: the commanded current means a sink-sustained root, zero means a state the compliance bound could never have deleted
